description: §6.7.1a — a multi-statement `on mount { }` body whose EXTENSION is the FIRST statement: `match @x { … }` then `@x = 5`. Because statement 1 (the match) parses as a clean leading exprNode, the fast path emitted ONLY the match and SILENTLY DROPPED the trailing `@x = 5` (S313 review #3). The reroute must fire for any multi-statement body that needs structured lowering, not only when statement 1 fails to parse. Post-fix both statements run at mount: @x = 1 selects the `1` arm (@label = "one"), then @x = 5. No input — the boot/mount shape.
rationale: §6.7.1a sugar-equivalence — every statement of an `on mount` body must lower, regardless of order. With @x = 1 the match writes @label = "one"; the following `@x = 5` also executes (a dropped tail would leave @x = 1). Pinned on both cells so the tail-drop regression is caught.
